PROP
39
PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification. Fiscal Impact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements. Supporters: The Transparency Foundation; Latino American Political Assn; Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Assn; CA Women’s Leadership Assn Opponents: ACLU California Action; Common Cause; League of Women Voters of California
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Yes on Prop. 39 gives California a BIPARTISAN solution for VOTER ID. Supported by a solid majority of Democratic, Independent and Republican voters. Increases trust and confidence in our elections.
CON
No on Prop. 39. This would advance Trump’s voter suppression agenda by adding costly, unnecessary barriers that could block eligible California voters, expose personal information to identity theft, and waste hundreds of millions in taxpayer dollars. Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No.

## California Secretary of State Shirley N. Weber, Ph.D., Announces the Statewide Voter Information Guide for the November 3, 2026, General Election Is Available for Public Review
**Sacramento, Calif.** – Today California Secretary of State Shirley N. Weber, Ph.D., made the November 3, 2026, California General Election Official Voter Information Guide available for public review.
The guide, which will be mailed to every voting household in California, includes information about propositions and statements from candidates running for constitutional offices, as well as other important election information such as the California Voter Bill of Rights and information about how eligible Californians can vote.
California’s Official Voter Information Guide is available in 10 languages—English, Spanish, Chinese, Hindi, Japanese, Khmer, Korean, Tagalog, Thai, and Vietnamese.
The guide is available for public examination from July 21, 2026 through August 10, 2026 at https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/public-display and at the Office of the Secretary of State’s Sacramento and Los Angeles locations.
During this public display period, any elector can challenge any portion of the Official Voter Information Guide in Sacramento Superior Court.

# Proposition 39
Prohibits Citizens From Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification.
Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
## Analysis of Measure
### Background
***Elections Administration.*** County elections officials administer most elections in California.
As part of this work, they print and mail ballots and other voting materials to registered voters.
Some state agencies also have workload related to voting.
For example, the Secretary of State oversees elections across the state and prepares and mails the state *Voter Information Guide*.
...
To be eligible to register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, live in California, be at least 18 years old, not currently be in prison, and not be found unable to vote by a court.
...
People can register online through the Secretary of State’s website, by mail, in person at a county elections office, or through the California Department of Motor Vehicles.
A voter’s identity is established through the registration process by using their driver’s license number, state identification number, or last four digits of their Social Security number.
Voters who do not provide this identifying information through the registration process may be asked to present identification the first time they vote.

PROP
39
PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification. Fiscal Impact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements. Supporters: The Transparency Foundation; Latino American Political Assn; Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Assn; CA Women’s Leadership Assn Opponents: ACLU California Action; Common Cause; League of Women Voters of California
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Yes on Prop. 39 gives California a BIPARTISAN solution for VOTER ID. Supported by a solid majority of Democratic, Independent and Republican voters. Increases trust and confidence in our elections.
CON
No on Prop. 39. This would advance Trump’s voter suppression agenda by adding costly, unnecessary barriers that could block eligible California voters, expose personal information to identity theft, and waste hundreds of millions in taxpayer dollars. Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No.

YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.

PRO
Yes on Prop. 39 gives California a BIPARTISAN solution for VOTER ID. Supported by a solid majority of Democratic, Independent and Republican voters. Increases trust and confidence in our elections.
CON
No on Prop. 39. Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No.

# 2026 California Proposition 39
**Proposition 39**, also known as the **California voter ID initiative**, is an initiated constitutional amendment in the state of California that on November 3, 2026, will be on the ballot.
The initiative would amend the state constitution to require the use of a government-issued ID for in-person voting, as well as the last four digits of a unique government-issued ID number when casting a mail-in ballot.
The amendment would also require the state of California to provide free voter ID cards that can be used to cast a ballot, and would enforce the maintenance of accurate voter registration lists by the secretary of state and election officials.

**Proposition 39**, also known as the **California voter ID initiative**, is an initiated constitutional amendment in the state of California that on November 3, 2026, will be on the ballot.
The initiative would amend the state constitution to require the use of a government-issued ID for in-person voting, as well as the last four digits of a unique government-issued ID number when casting a mail-in ballot.

https://www.desertsun.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/10/30/california-propositions-election-night-updates/92432935007/
Oct. 30, 2026, 11:45 a.m.
PT
Voting is underway in California, where voters will decide on a slate of ballot measures.
Polls close at 8 p.m.
Tuesday.
However, it may remain unclear whether Tuesday night will bring California's ballot-measure results.
...
## Proposition 39: the Voter ID initiative
California is one of 14 states that do not require voters to present identification to cast a ballot.
According to the state's voter information guide, if passed by voters, Proposition 39 would:
- Require voters casting a mail-in ballot to provide a government-issued ID number.
- Invalidate mail ballots should the ID number on the ballot envelope not match the ID number used when registering.
- Require voters casting a ballot in person to show a government-issued ID.
...
Recent polling on Proposition 39 has shown the measure failing.
A UC Berkeley IGS poll released Oct. 29 found the Voter ID initiative trailing by a wide 20-percentage-point margin, with 57% of voters opposed and 37% in favor.
A Public Policy Institute of California Poll released a day earlier shows Proposition 39 with fewer than half of likely voters in support: 41% in favor and 58% opposed.

### Proposal
***Requires State and Local Elections Officials to Verify U.S. Citizenship Status of Registered Voters.*** Proposition 39 requires state and local elections officials to make “best efforts” using government data to verify that voters on the rolls are U.S. citizens.
Proposition 39 requires elections officials to report every year the percentage of registered voters in each county whose citizenship status has been verified.
***Requires Voters to Select Government-Issued Identification for Voting by Mail.*** Proposition 39 requires new and existing voters to select a government-issued identification in their voter registration to vote by mail.
***Requires Voters to Provide Additional Identifying Information to Vote.*** Proposition 39 requires voters to provide additional identifying information each time they cast a ballot in any election in California.

## Proposition 39: Requires government-issued identification to vote
Proposition 39 would amend the state Constitution to introduce new voter ID requirements for in-person and mail voting.
The measure would prohibit citizens from voting in elections unless they present government-issued identification that matches their voter registration.
The measure also includes requirements for election officials related to verifying citizenship.
A yes vote would establish the proposed identification and verification requirements.
A no vote would leave existing election rules in place.
Supporters say the measure would strengthen election security and increase public confidence in voting.
Opponents argue that the requirements could create barriers for eligible voters who lack the required documents and that existing safeguards already protect election integrity.

## Proposition 39: Requires government-issued identification to vote
Proposition 39 would amend the state Constitution to introduce new voter ID requirements for in-person and mail voting.
The measure would prohibit citizens from voting in elections unless they present government-issued identification that matches their voter registration.
The measure also includes requirements for election officials related to verifying citizenship.
A yes vote would establish the proposed identification and verification requirements.
A no vote would leave existing election rules in place.
Supporters say the measure would strengthen election security and increase public confidence in voting.
Opponents argue that the requirements could create barriers for eligible voters who lack the required documents and that existing safeguards already protect election integrity.

## Proposition 39: Requires government-issued identification to vote
Proposition 39 would amend the state Constitution to introduce new voter ID requirements for in-person and mail voting.
The measure would prohibit citizens from voting in elections unless they present government-issued identification that matches their voter registration.
The measure also includes requirements for election officials related to verifying citizenship.
A yes vote would establish the proposed identification and verification requirements.
A no vote would leave existing election rules in place.
Supporters say the measure would strengthen election security and increase public confidence in voting.
Opponents argue that the requirements could create barriers for eligible voters who lack the required documents and that existing safeguards already protect election integrity.

### Summary
The initiative received a revised ballot title and was approved for signature gathering on September 19, 2025.
To qualify for the ballot, proponents were required to collect 874,641 valid signatures.The campaign submitted nearly 1.37 million signatures on March 2, 2026 and the initiative officially qualified for the November 2026 ballot as Proposition 39 on April 24, 2026.
On July 27, 2026, Californians for Voter ID filed a lawsuit against the Secretary of State challenging the new ballot title for Proposition 39, which was drafted by Attorney General Rob Bonta after his office received the amendment.
The plaintiffs argued that the new title of “prohibits citizens from voting unless they present government-issued identification,” was false and misleading, as it did not include the original title’s reference to additional voter identification and citizenship verification requirements.
The Attorney General’s Office maintained that the revised language more accurately describes the measure’s provisions.
On August 6, 2026, Sacramento County Superior Court found for the state and ruled that the ballot title is sufficient, thus the measure will remain on the ballot unchanged.

### Summary
The initiative received a revised ballot title and was approved for signature gathering on September 19, 2025.
To qualify for the ballot, proponents were required to collect 874,641 valid signatures.The campaign submitted nearly 1.37 million signatures on March 2, 2026 and the initiative officially qualified for the November 2026 ballot as Proposition 39 on April 24, 2026.
On July 27, 2026, Californians for Voter ID filed a lawsuit against the Secretary of State challenging the new ballot title for Proposition 39, which was drafted by Attorney General Rob Bonta after his office received the amendment.
The plaintiffs argued that the new title of “prohibits citizens from voting unless they present government-issued identification,” was false and misleading, as it did not include the original title’s reference to additional voter identification and citizenship verification requirements.
The Attorney General’s Office maintained that the revised language more accurately describes the measure’s provisions.
On August 6, 2026, Sacramento County Superior Court found for the state and ruled that the ballot title is sufficient, thus the measure will remain on the ballot unchanged.

39
PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification. Fiscal Impact: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements. Supporters: The Transparency Foundation; Latino American Political Assn; Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Assn; CA Women’s Leadership Assn Opponents: ACLU California Action; Common Cause; League of Women Voters of California
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: A voter’s identity would continue to be established with the voter’s signature.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Yes on Prop. 39 gives California a BIPARTISAN solution for VOTER ID. Supported by a solid majority of Democratic, Independent and Republican voters. Increases trust and confidence in our elections.
CON
No on Prop. 39. This would advance Trump’s voter suppression agenda by adding costly, unnecessary barriers that could block eligible California voters, expose personal information to identity theft, and waste hundreds of millions in taxpayer dollars. Don’t let MAGA billionaires decide which voters count. Vote No.

Those results are in line with September polls from the Berkeley Institute for Governmental Studies and the Public Policy Institute of California, both of which had the measure losing by similar margins.

Independents favor the measure by a small margin, 45% to 41%.

## Proposition 39: Requires government-issued identification to vote
Proposition 39 would amend the state Constitution to introduce new voter ID requirements for in-person and mail voting.
The measure would prohibit citizens from voting in elections unless they present government-issued identification that matches their voter registration.
The measure also includes requirements for election officials related to verifying citizenship.
